title: Maxwell–Boltzmann and catalysts; Rate equations and orders
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Eduqas A-level Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: KN03#t3 term and clue written for the game; KN03#t4 term and clue written for the game; KN04#t3 term and clue written for the game; KN04#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: KN03#N.3a, KN04#N.3a, KN03#N.12, KN04#N.6a.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Catalyst
items.clue: Provides an alternative route with a lower barrier and is not used up.

items.label: Enzyme
items.clue: A biological molecule that speeds up a reaction, such as catalase in raw potato.

items.label: Rate equation
items.clue: Expression such as k[X][Y] that links how fast a reaction goes to concentrations.

items.label: Order
items.clue: The power to which a reactant's concentration is raised; found only by experiment.

questions.stem: Which energy profile correctly shows an endothermic reaction?

options.text: Products higher than reactants; Ea arrow from the reactants up to the peak; ΔH arrow from reactants up to products.
Products higher than reactants; Ea arrow from the products up to the peak.
Products lower than reactants; ΔH arrow pointing down; Ea arrow from reactants up to the peak.
Products higher than reactants; Ea arrow from the reactants up to the products level.

questions.explanation: Endothermic means products are higher in energy. Ea runs from the reactants to the top of the barrier; ΔH from reactants to products.

questions.stem: The rate equation for a reaction is rate = k[A][B]². At constant temperature, the concentrations of A and B are both doubled. By what factor does the rate increase?
questions.explanation: Doubling [A] gives ×2¹ = 2; doubling [B] gives ×2² = 4. The rate rises by 2 × 4 = 8.

questions.stem: A mixture of hydrogen and oxygen can stay unchanged at room temperature for years. In Döbereiner's lamp (1823), a jet of hydrogen in air strikes a piece of platinum and reacts at once, with no flame or spark to start it. Which explanation is correct?

options.text: The platinum heats the gas, so the curve moves to higher energy and more molecules exceed the same Ea.
The platinum gives a route with a lower Ea, so at the same temperature far more molecules have enough energy.
The platinum makes the reaction more exothermic, so the molecules gain the energy they need to react.
The platinum changes the shape of the curve, moving its peak to higher energy without heating.

questions.stem: The rate equation for a reaction is rate = k[A]², with concentrations in mol dm⁻³ and the rate in mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹. What are the units of k?

options.text: mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹, as the rate constant has the same units as the rate
mol⁻¹ dm³ s⁻¹, as k = rate/[A]² for a second-order reaction
s⁻¹, as only one reactant, A, appears in the rate equation
mol³ dm⁻⁹ s⁻¹, as k = rate × [A]² when the rate equation is rearranged

questions.explanation: (mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹)/(mol dm⁻³)² = mol⁻¹ dm³ s⁻¹, for any reaction that is second order overall.
